topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution toward cancer in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their influence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how evidence about that contribution should be interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations, sometimes through metabolic activation within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-driven initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete and recap the mechanistic account by showing how carcinogenic effects depend on the tissue and developmental context of exposure.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenic exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the methods available to establish links between exposures and cancer, emphasizing what their evidence can and cannot demonstrate.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing its conclusions and placing cancer risks in the context of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
